Recompute a region map by point in polygon

Source: R/region_map.R
rgnmappts.Rd

Assigns each point (a facility's longitude and latitude) to the polygon of a boundary file that contains it, and carries the polygon's identifier and name columns onto the result. Requires the sf package and a boundary file; returns NULL when either is absent, so a verification script can record the check as unavailable instead of failing for a missing optional dependency.

Usage

rgnmappts(x, y, unit, bounds, fields, crs = 4326)

Arguments

x, y

Longitude and latitude of each point (numeric vectors, no NA), in the coordinate reference system crs.

unit

Identifier for each point, same length (character, no missing or empty values).

bounds

Path to a boundary file sf can read (a shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, ...).

fields

Character vector of columns of the boundary file to carry onto the result.

crs

Coordinate reference system the points are in, anything sf::st_crs() accepts. Default 4326, that is WGS84, which is what published latitude and longitude columns almost always are.

Value

A data frame: unit, the requested fields (factors converted to character; NA for a point in no polygon, the first polygon's values for a point in several), and nreg (integer), the number of polygons that contained the point. Any value of nreg other than 1 is a failure – zero means the point fell outside the geography, more than one means the boundaries overlap – so it is returned rather than silently resolved. NULL if sf is not installed or boundaries does not exist.

Details

The points are projected onto the boundary file's own coordinate reference system before matching, never the other way round: a cartographic boundary file is published in a projection chosen for the country it covers, and reprojecting the polygons to compare them against unprojected points moves the edges. Containment is sf::st_within(), so a point exactly on a shared edge is in neither polygon. The whole boundary file is read into memory with sf::st_read(); national files can take some seconds.

Point in polygon is preferred to matching place names against subdivision names whenever both are available. Names fail on exactly the cases that matter and fail quietly: a facility in a community rather than an incorporated municipality, a city amalgamated into a larger one, a township absorbed by a neighbour. The geometry has no opinion about any of that.

rgnmapalt() checks this result against the name route, with those cases named, and rgnmapcmp() compares it with a published map.

Errors (when sf and the file are present): missing or empty unit; x, y and unit of different lengths; missing coordinates; a field the boundary file does not have.

See also

rgnmapcmp(), rgnmapalt()

Examples

# Two square regions as a small GeoJSON boundary file.
gj <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
writeLines(paste0(
  '{"type":"FeatureCollection","features":[',
  '{"type":"Feature","properties":{"CDUID":"A","CDNAME":"West"},"geometry":',
  '{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-80,43],[-79,43],[-79,44],[-80,44],[-80,43]]]}},',
  '{"type":"Feature","properties":{"CDUID":"B","CDNAME":"East"},"geometry":',
  '{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-79,43],[-78,43],[-78,44],[-79,44],[-79,43]]]}}]}'
), gj)

if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  obs <- rgnmappts(
    x = c(-79.5, -78.5, -70), y = c(43.5, 43.5, 43.5),
    unit = c("North Jail", "South Jail", "Far Jail"),
    bounds = gj, fields = c("CDUID", "CDNAME")
  )
  print(obs)
  # the point outside both regions is reported, not dropped
  obs$unit[obs$nreg != 1]

  # a field the file does not have is an error
  print(try(rgnmappts(-79.5, 43.5, "North Jail", gj, fields = "PRUID")))
}
#>         unit CDUID CDNAME nreg
#> 1 North Jail     A   West    1
#> 2 South Jail     B   East    1
#> 3   Far Jail  <NA>   <NA>    0
#> Error : boundary file has no column(s): PRUID
#> [1] "Error : boundary file has no column(s): PRUID\n"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "try-error"
#> attr(,"condition")
#> <simpleError: boundary file has no column(s): PRUID>

# no boundary file: NULL, so a script can record the check as unavailable
rgnmappts(-79.5, 43.5, "North Jail",
                       bounds = file.path(tempdir(), "missing.shp"), fields = "CDUID")
#> NULL
unlink(gj)
